note: Oral non-peptide GnRH antagonists (relugolix, linzagolix; opigolix stopped after phase 2) bind human and monkey but barely rat GnRHR, so macaque HPG-axis suppression and a human-GnRHR knock-in mouse stood in for disease models, a rat endometriosis implant model came late, and the oestradiol window and bone trade-off were built from human data.
label: Endometriosis (GnRH antagonists)

engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey HPG axis (castrated/OVX LH; intact-female E2 and menses)
engagement.note: Oral relugolix held LH down for >24 h at 3 mg/kg in castrated macaques; rodents unusable because relugolix barely binds rat GnRHR.
engagement.short: Relugolix suppresses LH in castrated macaques
engagement.quote: Oral administration of 16b maintained the suppressive effect of the plasma luteinizing hormone levels in castrated cynomolgus monkeys at a 3 mg/kg dose for more than 24 h.
engagement.judgement: One track for the whole monkey HPG programme: castrated/OVX-monkey LH (Miwa 2011 for relugolix; Tezuka 2022, 10.1111/1440-1681.13688, for linzagolix) and the intact-female E2/menstrual-cycle arm (Yselty EPAR) are the same species, drug and axis with graded readouts, not different systems. model_filed left null: the castrated-monkey LH study was not located by grep in the Myfembree nonclinical review, which lists only in-vitro monkey-receptor work.

engagement.model: Human-GnRHR knock-in mouse (uterine/prostate weight, oestrous arrest)
engagement.note: Relugolix 100 mg/kg BID put knock-in females into constant dioestrus and cut uterine weight to ovariectomised levels; wild-type mice unaffected.
engagement.short: Knock-in mouse: uterus to OVX weight
engagement.quote: In female knock-in mice, twice-daily oral administration of TAK-385 (100mg/kg) induced constant diestrous phases within the first week, decreased the uterus weight to ovariectomized levels and downregulated GnRH receptor mRNA in the pituitary after 4 weeks.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the same study (TAK-385-00103) is summarised in the FDA nonclinical review.
engagement.judgement: Separate track from the monkey: a different species engineered for the human receptor, with a downstream tissue readout (uterine and prostate weight) rather than LH. model_filed true: the Myfembree nonclinical review (2021) summarises studies TAK-385-00103/00105 in these mice.

engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkey HPG axis (castrated/OVX LH; intact-female E2 and menses)
engagement.note: First published human PD: oral relugolix 40-180 mg/d lowered LH and testosterone to castrate levels in healthy men, as the castrated-macaque LH readout predicted. Retrodiction by post-dating: GnRH-antagonist suppression of gonadotropins in women was public in 2008 (elagolix, Struthers 2008, doi 10.1210/jc.2008-1695) before this model result.
engagement.quote: Oral TAK-385 (40-180 mg/d) was well tolerated and effectively lowered testosterone in healthy men.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; PMC4667159 full text not retrievable through Europe PMC or efetch, so whether MacLean cites the macaque data is unverified. LH was a main outcome measure but only the testosterone result is quotable from the abstract.
engagement.reason: Macaque LH suppression matched in men
engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of LH/testosterone suppression; monkey 3 mg/kg single dose and human 40-180 mg/d were not scaled to each other
engagement.judgement: Healthy volunteers count for engagement. Phase 1 registry record not looked up (UK 2012-13 study; no NCT in the abstract), registry_date null. Testosterone is downstream of the receptor's own product (LH), hence readout_tier downstream. Linzagolix repeats the pairing later (OVX-monkey LH, Tezuka 2022; E2 suppression in patients, Donnez 2020) and the EPAR describes both sides, but 2015 is the earliest public comparison for a member drug.

engagement.model: Human-GnRHR knock-in mouse (uterine/prostate weight, oestrous arrest)
engagement.note: Male knock-in mice dosed to castrate prostate weight; in men, relugolix >=80 mg/d gave sustained castrate testosterone within days. Retrodiction by post-dating: GnRH-antagonist suppression of gonadotropins in women was public in 2008 (elagolix, Struthers 2008, doi 10.1210/jc.2008-1695) before this model result.
engagement.short: Mouse castration readout matched in men
engagement.quote: TAK-385 doses ≥ 80 mg/d achieved sustained medical castration and trough TAK-385 concentrations >4 ng/mL.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the paper's citation of the knock-in mouse work is unverified.
engagement.reason: Mouse castration readout matched in men
engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of gonadal suppression; mouse 3 mg/kg BID (males) vs human 80 mg/d, exposures not compared
engagement.judgement: Nakata 2014: 'The same dose of TAK-385 also reduced the prostate weight to castrate levels in male knock-in mice.' The matching human readout is castrate testosterone in MacLean 2015, so the mouse track gets its own same entry on the same source; the female readout (uterine weight, dioestrus) is matched by amenorrhoea and E2 suppression in women but is scored under efficacy.

engagement.confidence_note: EPAR p.18 read from the full text (pdftotext); 'supressed' is the EPAR's spelling. The run date of Kissei's rat PD studies is not public and the Tezuka 2022 abstract (10.1111/1440-1681.13688) reports monkeys only, so 2022 is first public, not first use.
engagement.note: Linzagolix (rat GnRHR Ki 274 nM, unlike relugolix) suppressed LH in male rats and E2 in pro-oestrus female rats; first public in the EPAR.
engagement.short: Linzagolix lowers LH and E2 in rats
engagement.quote: In vivo, linzagolix supressed LH secretion in a dose-dependent manner in male rats and castrated male as well as ovariectomized female monkeys. Similarly, E2 secretion was dose-dependently inhibited in pro-oestrus female rats.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry. A rat HPG system is a different species from the draft's cynomolgus HPG track and a different model and prediction from the rat autotransplant endometriosis track, so it is its own track; the context note's 'barely rat GnRHR' holds for relugolix only.
engagement.model: Rat HPG axis (LH in male rats; E2 in pro-oestrus female rats), linzagolix

engagement.magnitude_basis: serum E2 suppression, dose-dependent in rat and in women; no exposure threshold quoted for the rat
engagement.confidence_note: Pairing made by me, not stated: EPAR p.18 (rat) and p.52 (clinical primary pharmacology, pooled over phase 1 women and fibroid/endometriosis patients) sit in one document but are never set side by side. Donnez 2024 (EDELWEISS 3) restates the endometriosis phase 2 E2 result (<20 pg/mL at 200 mg; 20-60 pg/mL at 75-100 mg).
engagement.note: Rat E2 suppression carried to women: linzagolix 100 and 200 mg rapidly took E2 below 20 pg/mL in the pooled clinical PD studies. Retrodiction by post-dating: GnRH-antagonist suppression of gonadotropins in women was public in 2008 (elagolix, Struthers 2008, doi 10.1210/jc.2008-1695) before this model result.
engagement.short: Rat E2 suppression seen in women
engagement.quote: Overall, linzagolix at 100 mg and 200 mg rapidly reduced E2 to the levels below 20 pg/mL.
engagement.reason: Rat E2 suppression seen in women
engagement.judgement: Class-level engagement: the rat's downstream readout (serum E2) fell dose-dependently in dosed humans. Direction only, since no rat exposure threshold for E2 is quoted, unlike the monkey Clast >20 ug/mL on the cyno track. Dated 2022 as the earliest document carrying both sides.
engagement.model: Rat HPG axis (LH in male rats; E2 in pro-oestrus female rats), linzagolix

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey HPG axis (castrated/OVX LH; intact-female E2 and menses)
dose.note: Macaque gave only an LH-suppressing oral dose (3 mg/kg); no human exposure target was stated, and relugolix 40 mg came from human dose-ranging.
dose.short: Dose set by human titration, not macaque
dose.quote: Oral administration of 16b maintained the suppressive effect of the plasma luteinizing hormone levels in castrated cynomolgus monkeys at a 3 mg/kg dose for more than 24 h.
dose.judgement: Relugolix's clinical dose was found by human dose-response (Osuga 2021: 10, 20, 40 mg vs placebo and leuprorelin), not derived from the macaque; no source relates the 3 mg/kg monkey dose to a human exposure.

dose.model: Human-GnRHR knock-in mouse (uterine/prostate weight, oestrous arrest)
dose.note: Females needed 100 mg/kg twice daily; no exposure or PK target was reported, so nothing to set against the 40 mg human dose.
dose.quote: In female knock-in mice, twice-daily oral administration of TAK-385 (100mg/kg) induced constant diestrous phases within the first week, decreased the uterus weight to ovariectomized levels and downregulated GnRH receptor mRNA in the pituitary after 4 weeks.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the FDA nonclinical review confirms 100 mg/kg BID as the effective female dose and 30 mg/kg as no-effect, without exposures.
dose.judgement: A mg/kg dose without PK is not an exposure target under the dose rules; left untested rather than scaled by hand.

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (39-week; dog added for linzagolix)
dose.note: Monkey NOAEL 15 mg/kg gave a stated 26x AUC margin over the 40 mg human dose; patients reached full suppression without the monkey liver toxicity. Retrodiction: the monkey NOAEL margin was first public in the 2021 FDA review, after relugolix's own patient dosing (Osuga 2020); dose ruling counts only the same drug's patient result, and it does here.
dose.short: 26x monkey liver margin held at 40 mg
dose.quote: In a 39-week study in monkeys, a NOAEL was established at 15 mg/kg (5198 ng*h/mL AUC; 26X the MRHD).
dose.confidence_note: Review is for the uterine-fibroid NDA; the 40 mg dose and its hepatic safety carry to endometriosis (SPIRIT 1/2 abstract lists no liver signal; Osuga 2021 none). Myfembree later carried a transaminase warning from its E2/NETA component, not read here.
dose.magnitude_basis: 26x AUC margin from the monkey NOAEL to the 40 mg MRHD, as stated by the reviewer; liver toxicity and systemic phospholipidosis appeared at 50 mg/kg (99x)
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the model stated a tolerated exposure above the effective one and patients were dosed to target (40 mg; 100% suppression regimen) without that toxicity, so dose is same with margin_stated. The reviewer's margin is to the MRHD, which is the comparison, hence comparison_stated true. Phospholipidosis had no monkey NOAEL (minimal at 1.1x) and was 'not observed in clinical studies', but it was not looked for in patients, so it is not scored as an over-prediction. Tox study dates are not public, model_first_use_year null. A separate track from the castrated-monkey PD model: intact animals, toxicology endpoints, a different prediction.

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey HPG axis (castrated/OVX LH; intact-female E2 and menses)
dose.note: Intact-female monkeys set >~20 ug/mL serum linzagolix for complete ovarian inhibition; in women 200 mg gave E2 <20 pg/mL in all subjects and pain responded. Retrodiction: the monkey Clast threshold was first public in the 2022 EPAR, after linzagolix's own phase 2 E2 data (Donnez 2020).
dose.short: Monkey full-suppression target reached at 200 mg
dose.quote: For the 200 mg linzagolix alone regimen, 100% of subjects had E2 levels below 20 pg/mL at Week 4.
dose.confidence_note: The EPAR gives the monkey threshold (Clast >~20 ug/mL) and the human PD outcome but not the human Clast at 200 mg; the E2 sentence sits in the EPAR's endometriosis PD discussion without naming the trial (likely NCT02778399).
dose.reason: Monkey full-suppression target reached at 200 mg
dose.magnitude_basis: regimen target (complete ovarian suppression) reached at 200 mg and partial at 75-100 mg; exposure not compared because the human Clast is not stated
dose.judgement: Model side (same document): 'more than approximately 20 μg/mL of serum linzagolix in Clast was needed for complete inhibition of ovarian function.' The assessor does not put the two sentences together, so comparison_stated false with the EPAR as model_src. 'Reached, drug worked': Donnez 2020 responders at >=75 mg (NCT02778399, results 2022-07-21) and EDELWEISS 3 at 200 mg + add-back. The tolerability margin is scored once, on the toxicology track.

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (39-week; dog added for linzagolix)
dose.note: Linzagolix: monkey liver NOAEL margin <1 absolute, ~3x free drug at 200 mg; patients were dosed to full suppression with only mild, reversible LFT rises. Retrodiction: the monkey liver margin was first public in the 2022 EPAR, after linzagolix's own patient dosing (Donnez 2020).
dose.short: Thin monkey liver margin; 200 mg tolerated
dose.quote: In terms of absolute exposures, margins to NOAELs in monkey studies defined relative to effects observed on the liver based on organ weight changes and increases in serum liver enzymes are less than 1.
dose.confidence_note: EPAR is the uterine-fibroid MAA (PRIMROSE); the 200 mg regimen and LFT findings are the same as in the endometriosis trials but the quoted safety pool is fibroid patients.
dose.reason: Thin monkey liver margin; patients tolerated 200 mg
dose.magnitude_basis: monkey liver-effect NOAEL vs 200 mg steady-state exposure: <1x total, ~3x free; patients showed >3x ULN LFT rises in <1% and no Hy's law case
dose.judgement: Same status as the relugolix entry on this track, so strengthens. Decision 16 on the toxic end: the monkey put liver effects at or near the clinical exposure, patients reached the full-suppression dose and toxicity did not block it (mild AST/ALT rises, slightly above placebo, reversible), so not blocked_by toxicity; called same with source_calls_it partial because the absolute margin was misplaced. EPAR: 'However, these are ≈ 3-fold in terms of free drug.'

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The window was derived from and re-fitted to phase 1/2 human data; whether 75 mg held E2 in it in EDELWEISS 3 is in the full paper, not the abstract, so no status is given.
dose.note: Model's exposure target: E2 held in the 20-50 pg/mL window (AUC-driven), reached at 75-125 mg; phase 3 E2 at 75 mg not in the abstract.
dose.short: E2 window 20-50 pg/mL is the target
dose.quote: The previously-reported E2 target range (20-50 pg/mL) to balance efficacy and safety endpoints was confirmed.
dose.reason: E2 window target, phase 3 E2 unquoted
dose.judgement: Untested, not same: the dose table would tie dose to the efficacy partial match only if the exposure target were shown reached in phase 3, which the abstract does not state.
dose.model: Integrated PK-PD and systems-pharmacology model of linzagolix (E2, pelvic pain, bleeding, lumbar BMD) built from phase 1/2 data

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Wiley paywall). The EPAR (p.18) carries the rat endometriosis study, so model_filed true, but not the ~1 umol/L free target. No endometriosis trial reports free linzagolix concentrations to set against it; human unbound fraction is ~0.1% (EPAR hepatic-impairment study), so any comparison would be my own arithmetic.
dose.note: Rat autotransplant model stated an effective free last-observed linzagolix concentration of ~1 umol/L; no patient free-exposure comparison has been published.
dose.short: Rat states ~1 umol/L free effective level
dose.quote: The effective concentration of linzagolix, calculated as the free form of the last-observed drug concentration, was ~1 μmol/L in endometriosis model rats.
dose.judgement: Opening dose entry on the existing rat track: the model states an exposure target, but no source compares it with human free exposure, so untested rather than same; deriving human free Clast from total levels and fu would be my own arithmetic.
dose.model: Rat surgically induced (autotransplant) endometriosis, implant volume
Cynomolgus monkey HPG axis (castrated/OVX LH; intact-female E2 and menses)
dose.note: Opener of the monkey HPG track for linzagolix: intact-female monkeys needed Clast above ~20 ug/mL for complete ovarian inhibition (EPAR; Tezuka 2022, doi 10.1111/1440-1681.13688).
dose.short: Monkey sets linzagolix Clast for full suppression
dose.quote: more than approximately 20 μg/mL of serum linzagolix in Clast was needed for complete inhibition of ovarian function.
dose.confidence_note: EPAR p.18 sentence as verified in the check record.
dose.judgement: Opening entry for the linzagolix track on the monkey system (split ruling); first public use for linzagolix is the EPAR of 22 Apr 2022, before Tezuka 2022 (epub 2022-07-12).

efficacy.model: Cynomolgus monkey HPG axis (castrated/OVX LH; intact-female E2 and menses)
efficacy.note: No disease readout: the macaque gives LH suppression only, so efficacy rode on the class's oestrogen-deprivation hypothesis from GnRH agonists.
efficacy.short: LH surrogate only; no disease model
efficacy.quote: Compound 16b is currently under clinical development with the code name of TAK-385.
efficacy.reason: Model readout is LH, not pain
efficacy.judgement: Kept untested on this track: the monkey predicts gonadotropin suppression, not pain, and crediting it with the pain result would score the hormonal hypothesis, not the model. Opigolix (ASP1707) has no published model: TERRA phase 2 (NCT01767090, Hum Reprod 2019, 10.1093/humrep/dez028) 'significantly reduced endometriosis-associated pelvic pain in a dose-related manner' and the programme was not taken further; patient-side only, so it scores nothing.

efficacy.model: Human-GnRHR knock-in mouse (uterine/prostate weight, oestrous arrest)
efficacy.note: Uterine weight fell to ovariectomised levels in knock-in females; the paper names endometriosis as a target but tests no lesion.
efficacy.short: Uterine weight to OVX levels in mice
efficacy.quote: TAK-385 may provide useful therapeutic interventions in hormone-dependent diseases including endometriosis, uterine fibroids and prostate cancer.
efficacy.judgement: The uterine-atrophy readout is an oestrogen-deprivation surrogate in a hormone-dependent tissue, the closest thing to a disease readout relugolix had, which is why this track and not the monkey carries the efficacy comparison.

efficacy.model: Rat surgically induced (autotransplant) endometriosis, implant volume
efficacy.note: Class proxy SKI2670 (never a member) shrank rat ectopic implants: first use of a disease model for oral GnRH antagonists. Opens the linzagolix track of the rat model with the proxy SKI2670; linzagolix itself was first run in it per the 2022 EPAR.
efficacy.quote: Finally, it exhibited regressive effects on ectopic implants in a rat endometriosis model without bone loss.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; proxy compound SKI2670 is not a tile member and never reached patients.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the rat track with a proxy, as the dating rule allows; the first member drug in this model is linzagolix (EPAR 2022, Tezuka 2023). Kim's 'without bone loss' claim for the proxy is not scored.

efficacy.model: Human-GnRHR knock-in mouse (uterine/prostate weight, oestrous arrest)
efficacy.note: Relugolix 10/20/40 mg cut endometriosis pelvic-pain VAS dose-dependently (-6.2/-8.1/-10.4 vs -3.8 mm placebo), 40 mg matching leuprorelin. Retrodiction by post-dating: a GnRH antagonist (cetrorelix) had already relieved endometriosis symptoms in patients (Kupker 2002, doi 10.1016/s1472-6483(10)61590-8) before this model result.
efficacy.quote: Oral administration of relugolix alleviated endometriosis-associated pain in a dose-response manner and was generally well tolerated.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. NCT01458301 has no posted results, registry_date null. Phase 3 confirmation: SPIRIT 1/2 (Lancet 2022) and the Japanese non-inferiority trial vs leuprorelin (Osuga 2022).
efficacy.reason: Mouse HPG suppression; pain fell dose-dependently
efficacy.magnitude_basis: pelvic-pain VAS change vs mouse uterine weight: different quantities, direction only

patient_trials.quote: In SPIRIT 1, 158 (75%) of 212 patients in the relugolix combination therapy group met the dysmenorrhoea responder criteria compared with 57 (27%) of 212 patients in the placebo group (treatment difference 47·6% [95% CI 39·3-56·0]; p<0·0001).

In SPIRIT 2, 155 (75%) of 206 patients in the relugolix combination therapy group were dysmenorrhoea responders compared with 62 (30%) of 204 patients in the placebo group (treatment difference 44·9% [95% CI 36·2-53·5]; p<0·0001).
Relugolix was noninferior to LEU for treating endometriosis-associated pelvic pain.

efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison: the mouse paper predicted usefulness in endometriosis from uterine atrophy; the first endometriosis trial's primary endpoint (pelvic-pain VAS) responded dose-dependently. Year 2020 is the epub date, the earliest public patient result (SPIRIT 1/2 and NCT03931915 have no posted registry results; SPIRIT was registered 2017 and published June 2022).

efficacy.model: Rat surgically induced (autotransplant) endometriosis, implant volume
efficacy.note: Linzagolix shrank rat endometrial implants at 50 mg/kg BID; in women, overall-pelvic-pain responders rose from 34.5% (placebo) to 56-62% at >=75 mg. Retrodiction by post-dating: a GnRH antagonist (cetrorelix) had already relieved endometriosis symptoms in patients (Kupker 2002, doi 10.1016/s1472-6483(10)61590-8) before this model result.
efficacy.short: Rat implants shrank; patients' pain responded
efficacy.quote: Compared with placebo, doses ≥ 75 mg resulted in a significantly greater proportion of responders for overall pelvic pain at 12 weeks (34.5%, 61.5%, 56.4%, and 56.3% for placebo, 75, 100, and 200 mg, respectively).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Donnez 2020 and for Tezuka 2023 (Wiley paywall). The run date of Kissei's rat study is not public; it sits in the MAA primary-pharmacodynamics package and is treated as prospective. If it was run after the 2018 phase 2b readout it is a retrodiction and this entry should read retro.
efficacy.reason: Rat implants shrank; patients' pain responded
efficacy.magnitude_basis: pain responder rate vs rat implant volume: different quantities, direction only

patient_trials.quote: Linzagolix significantly reduced EAP and improved QoL at doses of 75-200 mg and decreased BMD dose-dependently.

At 3 months, the daily 200 mg linzagolix dose with ABT met the primary efficacy objective, showing clinically meaningful and statistically significant reductions in dysmenorrhea and non-menstrual pelvic pain, with stable or decreased use of analgesics.

efficacy.judgement: Year 2022 is when the model side became public (EPAR: 'In a rat endometriosis model, linzagolix significantly reduced the volume of endometrial implants at 50 mg/kg BID'); the patient side (Donnez 2020, NCT02778399) was already out, so the pairing dates to the EPAR, with Donnez as src because its sentence carries the status. Tezuka 2023 (10.1111/1440-1681.13778, epub 2023-04-26) is the peer-reviewed model paper: 'Linzagolix significantly decreased cyst volumes compared with the control group at doses of 50 mg/kg or more.' EDELWEISS 3 (2024) met its co-primary endpoints at 200 mg + add-back; 75 mg alone met dysmenorrhoea only; EDELWEISS 2 was terminated and changes nothing.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMC9306723 is open access but was not read in full). The model was fitted to EDELWEISS 1 (phase 2, 2018 readout), so its phase 2 agreement is a fit, not a prediction; the opener carries no status.
efficacy.note: Model fitted to phase 1/2 data predicted 75-125 mg daily would meet pain and BMD targets; EDELWEISS 3 then tested 75 mg alone.
efficacy.short: Model picks 75-125 mg for pain and bone
efficacy.quote: Linzagolix once daily doses between 75-125 mg daily were expected to meet endometriosis-associated pain, efficacy, and BMD loss targets in Caucasian patients.
efficacy.judgement: In-silico track opened under the brief's 'QSP models used to choose doses'. The FLT3 tile left out an exposure-response model built on patient data; this one made a falsifiable prospective dose claim that phase 3 then tested, so it is listed and flagged for the adjudicator to drop if the precedent is preferred.
efficacy.model: Integrated PK-PD and systems-pharmacology model of linzagolix (E2, pelvic pain, bleeding, lumbar BMD) built from phase 1/2 data

efficacy.magnitude_basis: responder direction at 75 mg; the model gives odds per E2 change, the trial responder proportions
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Pairing by me: Donnez 2024 does not cite the model. EDELWEISS 3 primary completion (2021-10-18) preceded the model's publication (epub 2022-01-13), but the 75 mg-alone arm was fixed at trial start (2019-06) on the same analysis, so the prediction is treated as prospective; if a topline release predates 2022-01-13 the entry should read retro. Topline release date 2022-01-06 taken from the check record; the release itself was not re-read.
efficacy.note: 75 mg alone met the dysmenorrhoea co-primary but not NMPP at 3 months; 200 mg + add-back met both, as the model's E2 window implied. Co-primary design: at 75 mg dysmenorrhoea responders 44.0% vs 23.5% (P<0.001) were met and NMPP was not (P=0.279); the authors do not call the arm a failure, so scored as a partial match. Retrodiction: the model went online 2022-01-13, a week after ObsEva's EDELWEISS 3 topline release (2022-01-06), so the comparison dates to 2022.
efficacy.short: 75 mg hit dysmenorrhoea only; partial match
efficacy.quote: Combining 200 mg linzagolix with ABT was found to significantly reduce dysmenorrhea and non-menstrual pelvic pain at 3 months of therapy, while a daily dose of 75 mg linzagolix yielded a significant decrease only in dysmenorrhea at 3 months.
efficacy.reason: 75 mg hit dysmenorrhoea only; partial match
efficacy.judgement: Same with partial: the model said 75-125 mg meets pain targets; at 75 mg one of two co-primaries (dysmenorrhoea) was met and NMPP was not, in line with the model's own weak NMPP odds (1.07 per E2 50 to 20 pg/mL). The alternative reading, contra at 75 mg because 200 mg + ABT was needed for both endpoints, is noted; partial agreement is same under the brief.

patient_trials.quote: At 3 months, the daily 200 mg linzagolix dose with ABT met the primary efficacy objective, showing clinically meaningful and statistically significant reductions in dysmenorrhea and non-menstrual pelvic pain, with stable or decreased use of analgesics.

efficacy.model: Integrated PK-PD and systems-pharmacology model of linzagolix (E2, pelvic pain, bleeding, lumbar BMD) built from phase 1/2 data

efficacy.population: Unselected (prediction stratifies by lesion PR status)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Dosed with cetrorelix, a peptide GnRHR antagonist outside the tile's member list and modality (product_in_model false; modality left null because 'peptide' is not in this tile's modality_groups). The prospective validation the paper claims is for progestin response, not for GnRH antagonism.
efficacy.note: Patient lesions grafted into mice: low-PR lesions shrank on cetrorelix, not MPA; no member drug and no PR-stratified patient response to GnRH antagonism exist.
efficacy.short: PR status predicts lesion response in avatars
efficacy.quote: Low-PR lesions respond far more completely to GnRH antagonist than to MPA.
efficacy.reason: Avatar prediction awaits a member comparison
efficacy.judgement: Opened as an untested patient-level track by the same logic as the draft's SKI2670 rat opener: a sibling GnRHR antagonist in the system, no member drug, no patient comparison. model_kind animal because a xenograft in a mouse is an in-vivo system and the enum has no PDX value.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived endometrioma xenograft 'murine avatars' in NOD/SCID mice (lesion size by lesion PR status; cetrorelix)

safety.model: Human-GnRHR knock-in mouse (uterine/prostate weight, oestrous arrest)
safety.note: Four-week knock-in mice (with OVX controls) showed no bone-density change; women on relugolix 10-40 mg lost bone mineral density dose-dependently. Retrodiction: the model's data were first public after this drug's own patient BMD result; failed to reproduce it, so contra.
safety.short: Mouse bone null; patients lost BMD
safety.quote: The major adverse events with relugolix were hot flush, metrorrhagia, menorrhagia, and irregular menstruation, and bone mineral density decrease in a dose-response manner
safety.confidence_note: Quote is the opening clause of a 42-word sentence, cut verbatim before the leuprorelin comparison. The OVX control also showed no bone change, so the 4-week readout was insensitive rather than a positive prediction of safety; scored contra because mice can show oestrogen-deficiency bone loss and the model's data said none.
safety.reason: Mouse bone null; patients lost BMD
safety.judgement: Model side, FDA nonclinical review study TAK-385-00103: 'No difference in cancellous or cortical bone density between intact, OVX and TAK-385-treated mice were observed.' The bone datum became public with the review (posted 2021-06-24), hence year 2021 although the patient paper is 2020. SPIRIT (2022) confirms: lumbar BMD -2.0% in the delayed-combination (monotherapy) arm vs +0.2% placebo. BMD loss was anticipated from human GnRH-agonist experience and pre-specified in every trial; the atlas scores the model, not the programme's foresight.

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (39-week; dog added for linzagolix)
safety.note: 39-week monkeys predicted cessation of menses and liver toxicity only at 99x the human dose, with no bone readout; patients lost BMD dose-dependently. Retrodiction: the model's data were first public after this drug's own patient BMD result; failed to reproduce it, so contra.
safety.short: Monkey tox silent on BMD loss
safety.quote: The major adverse events with relugolix were hot flush, metrorrhagia, menorrhagia, and irregular menstruation, and bone mineral density decrease in a dose-response manner
safety.confidence_note: Quote cut verbatim from a 42-word sentence. On-target hypo-oestrogenic effects the monkey did predict (cessation of menses, uterine atrophy) matched amenorrhoea and hot flushes in patients; the miss is bone, which a 39-week monkey study could have measured and did not.
safety.judgement: FDA review: 'Females demonstrated decreased corpora lutea, decreased uterine weights, and cessation of menses.' No bone endpoint appears in the monkey summary. Suicidal ideation (nine reports in SPIRIT) is a harm no animal here could show and is not a miss. Phospholipidosis in monkeys was not seen clinically but was not looked for, so not scored as an over-prediction (see dose).

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (39-week; dog added for linzagolix)
safety.note: Linzagolix: monkey/dog liver-enzyme prediction held (mild AST/ALT rises, no Hy's law), but tox was again silent on bone; spine BMD fell 2.6% at 200 mg. Retrodiction: the model's data were first public after this drug's own patient BMD result; failed to reproduce it, so contra.
safety.short: Tox blind to BMD loss; liver held
safety.quote: Mean BMD loss (spine) at 24 weeks was <1% at doses of 50 and 75 mg and increased in a dose-dependent fashion up to 2.6% for 200 mg.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Donnez 2020. The liver comparison is the assessor's own in the fibroid EPAR (PRIMROSE pool); the bone datum is from endometriosis patients, so imported_from is not set.
safety.reason: Tox blind to BMD loss; liver held
safety.judgement: Second drug, same track, same status: strengthens. The EPAR states the liver side itself: 'Linzagolix in non-clinical studies (in dogs and monkeys), showed an increase in serum liver enzyme activity, and increase in serum lipid parameters with associated increase of liver weight.' and 'When AST/ALT are considered together all linzagolix arms had slightly higher rates than placebo'; that prediction held, hence source_calls_it partial. The EPAR nonclinical sections (9-month monkey, 6-month rat) mention no bone endpoint, so the track stays contra on BMD; a hit on one harm does not lift a miss on the class's main harm. Year 2022 is when the linzagolix model side became public.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The BMD model was 'adjusted to the clinical data' (phase 2), so the phase 2 BMD agreement is a fit. EDELWEISS 3 BMD at 75 mg alone is in the full paper; the abstract gives no number, so no status.
safety.note: QSP bone model predicted week-24 lumbar BMD loss of 0.09% (50 mg), 1.30% (100 mg), 2.67% (200 mg); no prospective BMD comparison quotable.
safety.short: Bone model predicts dose-graded BMD loss
safety.quote: The mean week 24 lumbar spine BMD change from baseline ranged from -0.092% in the 50 mg dose, -1.30% in the 100 mg dose group and -2.67% in the 200 mg dose group.
safety.reason: BMD prediction stated, not yet compared
safety.judgement: Opened in safety because the model states a harm prediction (dose-graded BMD loss) that the figure should show as existing; scoring waits on a quotable prospective BMD number.
safety.model: Integrated PK-PD and systems-pharmacology model of linzagolix (E2, pelvic pain, bleeding, lumbar BMD) built from phase 1/2 data
Rat surgically induced (autotransplant) endometriosis, implant volume
safety.note: Passing tolerability claim, now a safety prediction: the proxy GnRH antagonist SKI2670 regressed rat implants 'without bone loss'.
safety.short: Proxy shrinks implants without bone loss
safety.quote: Finally, it exhibited regressive effects on ectopic implants in a rat endometriosis model without bone loss.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; proxy compound SKI2670 is not a tile member and never reached patients.
safety.judgement: Passing-tolerability ruling: a no-bone-loss statement in an efficacy paper is the model's safety prediction. Proxy drug, so product_in_model false; attached to linzagolix, the member later run in this rat model.

safety.model: Rat surgically induced (autotransplant) endometriosis, implant volume
safety.note: Proxy rat model claimed no bone loss; women on linzagolix lost spine BMD dose-dependently, 2.6% at 200 mg in EDELWEISS (phase 2b).
safety.short: Rat said no bone loss; women lost BMD
safety.quote: Mean BMD loss (spine) at 24 weeks was <1% at doses of 50 and 75 mg and increased in a dose-dependent fashion up to 2.6% for 200 mg.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level on both sides; the rat dose and bone measure behind Kim's claim were not read.
safety.magnitude_basis: rat: no bone loss stated (proxy SKI2670); patients: dose-graded spine BMD loss up to 2.6% at 24 weeks
safety.judgement: Prospective: SKI2670 has no patient result of its own, so under the drug-specific safety rule nothing earlier makes the 2015 claim a retrodiction. Patients of this disease were measured. Proxy, so product_in_model false.
